newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BOARD OF GOVERNORS APPROVES EXPANSION TO FOUR U.S. CITIES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BOARD OF GOVERNORS APPROVES EXPANSION TO FOUR U.S. CITIES.

text.p: The National Hockey League's board of governor's Wednesday awarded new franchises to groups in Atlanta, Nashville, Tennessee, St. Paul, Minnesota and Columbus, Ohio.
The Nashville franchise will begin play in 1998, and Atlanta in 1999, while the teams in St. Paul and Columbus will join the league in 2000, the NHL announced.
The expansion will boost NHL membership to 30 teams by the end of the cycle. Each new ownership group must pay an $80 million franchise fee.
The league's expansion committee recommended the four cities last week. It had also considered bids from Houston and Oklahoma City groups.
Each new franchise must sell 12,000 season tickets by four months before the start of their first season, NHL commissioner Gary Bettman noted.
The board of governors also approved the relocation of the former Hartford Whalers franchise to North Carolina for the 1997-98 season. It has been renamed the Carolina Hurricanes.
